column5: He likes buying brand-name clothes.
column6: 名牌 is a famous brand: 名牌衣服 (brand-name clothes), 名牌大学 (a top university). It can be a product or a school.

column5: This is my business card.
column6: 名片 is a business card: 一张名片, 递名片 (to hand over a card), 交换名片 (to exchange cards).

column4: 请给我一个明确的回答。
column5: Please give me a clear answer.
column6: 明确 means clear and definite, with no doubt left: 明确的回答, 明确目标 (to set a clear goal). It can also be a verb: to make clear.

column5: His progress is very obvious.
column6: 明显 means obvious, easy to notice: 明显的变化 (an obvious change), 很明显 (it is obvious), 不明显 (not obvious).

column4: 他是一个有名的电影明星。
column5: He is a famous film star.
column6: 明星 is a star in the public eye: 电影明星 (a film star), 体育明星 (a sports star).

column5: The doctor saved his life.
column6: 命 is life: 救命 (to save a life; also a cry for help), 生命 (life), 一条命 (a life). It also means fate.

column4: 每个人都想改变自己的命运。
column5: Everyone wants to change their own fate.
column6: 命运 is fate: 改变命运 (to change one's fate), 命运不好 (an unlucky fate), 国家的命运 (the fate of a country).

column5: Do not touch it; that is very hot.
column6: 摸 is to touch with the hand: 摸一摸 (to feel), 摸头 (to pat on the head). 碰 is to bump into something by accident.

column5: This photo is very blurry.
column6: 模糊 means unclear or blurred: 模糊的照片, 记忆模糊 (a vague memory).

column4: 现在有很多新的工作模式。
column5: Now there are many new ways of working.
column6: 模式 is a standard way or pattern of doing something: 工作模式 (a working mode), 新模式 (a new model), 飞行模式 (flight mode on a phone).

column5: I am very unfamiliar with this city.
column6: 陌生 means unfamiliar: 陌生人 (a stranger), 陌生的地方 (an unfamiliar place), 对……很陌生. The opposite is 熟悉.

column5: I have seen you somewhere.
column6: 某 means "a certain" or "some" when you do not name the person or thing: 某人 (a certain person), 某个地方 (a certain place), 某天 (one day).

column5: Everyone's eyes are on him.
column6: 目光 is a look or gaze: 大家的目光 (everyone's eyes), 吸引目光 (to catch people's eyes).

column5: This table is made of wood.
column6: 木头 is wood or a piece of wood: 一块木头, 木头做的 (made of wood).

column5: Even if it rains, I will go.
column6: 哪怕 means "even if" and usually goes with 也 or 都 in the second part: 哪怕……也……. It shows a strong decision.

column5: An opportunity like this is rare.
column6: 难得 means hard to get, so rare and precious: 难得的机会 (a rare chance). Before a verb it means "seldom": 难得休息 (to rarely rest).

column5: The difficulty of this question is very great.
column6: 难度 is how hard something is: 难度大 (very difficult), 增加难度 (to raise the difficulty). 难 is "hard"; 难度 is the degree.

column5: His words are hard to believe.
column6: 难以 means "hard to" and goes before a verb: 难以相信 (hard to believe), 难以理解 (hard to understand). It is more formal than 很难.

column5: This man is a doctor.
column6: 男子 is a man, used in writing: 男子比赛 (a men's competition), 一名男子 (a man). 男人 is the everyday word.

column5: It is too noisy in the classroom.
column6: 闹 means "noisy" (很闹), "to make a noise" (别闹了) and "to play around" (闹着玩). 热闹 is "lively".

column5: The alarm clock did not ring, and I was late.
column6: 闹钟 is an alarm clock: 定闹钟 (to set an alarm), 闹钟响了 (the alarm goes off).

column5: The inside of this house is very large.
column6: 内部 is the inside of an organisation or thing: 公司内部 (inside the company), 内部结构 (internal structure).

column5: She is a very capable person.
column6: 能干 means able and good at getting things done: 又聪明又能干 (both clever and capable). 能 here is part of the word.

column5: He went abroad at the start of the year.
column6: 年初 is the start of the year: 年初的计划 (the plan at the start of the year). The end of the year is 年底.

column5: In those days, there were few telephones.
column6: 年代 is an era or a decade: 那个年代 (in those days), 九十年代 (the 1990s), 年代久远 (from long ago).

column5: He is not young any more.
column6: 年纪 is a person's age, mostly used for older people: 年纪大 (old), 年纪小 (young), 多大年纪 (how old). It is not used for things.

column5: Mum is preparing the New Year's Eve dinner.
column6: 年夜饭 is the big family dinner on the night before the Spring Festival: 吃年夜饭 (to have the New Year's Eve dinner).

column3: to read aloud; to study; to miss
column5: The teacher is reading the text aloud.
column6: 念 is to read aloud (念课文), to study (念书) and to miss someone (想念).

column5: He is wearing an old pair of jeans.
column6: 牛仔裤 are jeans: 一条牛仔裤. 牛仔 is a cowboy and 裤子 are trousers.

column5: This coffee is too strong.
column6: 浓 means strong or thick: 浓茶 (strong tea), 浓咖啡 (strong coffee), 味道很浓 (a strong smell). The opposite is 淡.

column5: The farmers are working in the fields.
column6: 农民 is a farmer: 一位农民, 很多农民 (many farmers). 农 means farming.

column4: 农业对这个国家很重要。
column5: Agriculture is very important for this country.
column6: 农业 is agriculture: 农业国家 (an agricultural country), 发展农业 (to develop agriculture).

column5: This woman is a teacher.
column6: 女子 is a woman, used in writing: 女子比赛 (a women's competition), 一名女子 (a woman). 女人 is the everyday word.

column5: Oh, I understand now.
column6: 哦 is read ò when you suddenly understand or agree: 哦，我知道了. In other tones it can show doubt or surprise.

column5: He has been to many European countries.
column6: 欧洲 is Europe: 欧洲国家 (European countries), 去欧洲 (to go to Europe).

column5: We met by chance.
column6: 偶然 means by chance, not planned: 偶然的机会 (a chance opportunity), 偶然认识 (to meet by chance).

column5: They are filming a movie here.
column6: 拍摄 is to shoot a film or a photo: 拍摄电影, 拍摄照片. 拍 is the everyday word, as in 拍照.

column4: 请把这些词按顺序排列。
column5: Please arrange these words in order.
column6: 排列 is to arrange in a row or in order: 排列顺序 (to arrange in order), 排列整齐 (neatly arranged).

column5: The company is sending him to work abroad.
column6: 派 is to send someone to do a job: 派人 (to send someone), 派他去 (to send him to). As a noun it means a group or school.

column4: 他丢了钱包，就去了派出所。
column5: He lost his wallet and went to the police station.
column6: 派出所 is the police station of a neighbourhood: 去派出所 (to go to the police station). It is the police office closest to where people live.

column5: The athletes are running on the track.
column6: 跑道 is a running track or an airport runway: 操场的跑道 (the track on a playground), 机场的跑道 (an airport runway).

column5: He broke the cup and has to pay compensation.
column6: 赔 is to pay for something you broke or lost: 赔钱 (to pay compensation; also to lose money in business), 赔一个 (to replace one).

column5: Children need their parents' company.
column6: 陪伴 is to keep someone company: 陪伴家人 (to be with family), 有你的陪伴 (with your company). 陪 is the everyday word.

column5: The company gives training to new people.
column6: 培训 is to train people for a job: 参加培训 (to attend training), 培训班 (a training class), 员工培训 (staff training). It is a verb and a noun.

column4: 父母要培养孩子的好习惯。
column5: Parents need to develop good habits in their children.
column6: 培养 is to develop a person's ability or habit over time: 培养习惯 (to build a habit), 培养人才 (to train talent), 培养兴趣 (to develop an interest).

column4: 这条裤子配这件衣服很好看。
column5: These trousers go very well with this top.
column6: 配 means "to match, go with" (配得上), "to mix or prepare" (配药) and "to deserve". 米饭配菜 (rice with dishes).

column4: 请大家配合我们的工作。
column5: Please everyone cooperate with our work.
column6: 配合 is to work together with someone, usually following their plan: 配合工作, 配合得很好 (to work well together). 合作 is between equal partners.

column5: The supermarket can deliver to your home.
column6: 配送 is to deliver goods to customers: 配送到家 (to deliver to your door), 免费配送 (free delivery), 配送费 (the delivery fee).

column5: He washes clothes in a basin.
column6: 盆 is a basin or a pot: 脸盆 (a washbasin), 花盆 (a flowerpot), 一盆花 (a pot of flowers).

column5: Be careful not to bump your head.
column6: 碰 is to bump into or touch, often by accident: 碰到 (to hit against), 碰头 (to meet up). 碰见 is to meet by chance.

column3: to run into; to meet by chance
column4: 我在路上碰见了老同学。
column5: I ran into an old classmate on the road.
column6: 碰见 is to meet someone by chance: 碰见朋友 (to run into a friend). 遇见 is similar but more written.

column5: A batch of new books has arrived.
column6: 批 is a measure word for a batch or group: 一批货 (a batch of goods), 一批学生. As a verb it means to approve or comment: 批准, 批评 (to criticise).

column5: The boss approved his plan.
column6: 批准 is to approve officially: 批准申请 (to approve an application), 得到批准 (to get approval).

column5: There is a horse on the grass.
column6: 匹 counts horses: 一匹马. It also counts rolls of cloth.

column5: Do not lie to me.
column6: 骗 is to cheat or to trick: 骗人 (to deceive people), 被骗 (to be cheated), 受骗 (to be deceived).

column3: to put together; to go all out
column4: 他把这些小块拼在一起。
column5: He puts these small pieces together.
column6: 拼 means "to put together" (拼起来) and "to go all out" (拼命, to risk one's all). It is also in 拼音 (pinyin).

column5: We first learn pinyin.
column6: 拼音 is pinyin, the system that writes Chinese sounds in letters: 学拼音 (to learn pinyin), 拼音输入 (to type with pinyin).

column5: These are all food products.
column6: 品 at the end of a word means a thing or product: 食品 (food), 产品 (a product), 作品 (a work), 商品 (goods). Alone it also means "to taste": 品茶.

column5: This brand is very famous.
column6: 品牌 is a brand: 新品牌 (a new brand), 品牌手机 (a brand-name phone). 名牌 is a famous brand.

column4: 这家商店的东西品质很好。
column5: The goods in this shop are of very good quality.
column6: 品质 is the quality of a thing: 品质好 (good quality). It also means a person's character: 良好的品质 (good qualities).

column5: There are many varieties of flowers here.
column6: 品种 is a variety or breed: 新品种 (a new variety), 品种多 (a wide range), 苹果的品种 (types of apple).

column5: The company has hired him as manager.
column6: 聘请 is to hire someone for a job or as an expert: 聘请老师 (to hire a teacher). It is formal; 请 here means "to invite".

column5: This road is very flat.
column6: 平 means flat or level: 平路 (a flat road), 放平 (to put level). It also means calm (平静) and equal (平均, 公平).

column4: 大家来评一评这个办法。
column5: Everyone, come and judge this method.
column6: 评 is to comment on and judge: 评一评 (to judge), 评价 (to evaluate). It is mostly used in words.

column3: to rely on; on the basis of
column4: 他凭自己的努力考上了大学。
column5: He got into university through his own effort.
column6: 凭 means "to rely on" (凭本事, by one's own skill) and "according to" (凭票入场, to enter by ticket). 凭什么？ means "on what grounds?"

column5: I wish you a safe journey.
column6: 平安 means safe and sound: 一路平安 (have a safe trip), 平安到家 (to arrive home safely). It is a word of blessing.

column5: When riding a bike, you must keep your balance.
column6: 平衡 is balance: 保持平衡 (to keep balance), 失去平衡 (to lose balance), 生活和工作的平衡 (work-life balance).

column4: 大家对这个电影的评价很高。
column5: Everyone thinks highly of this film.
column6: 评价 is to judge the value of something (verb) and the judgement itself (noun): 评价很高 (a high opinion), 高度评价 (to praise highly).

column3: to rely on; by means of
column4: 他凭借自己的努力成功了。
column5: He succeeded by relying on his own effort.
column6: 凭借 means to rely on something such as skill or an advantage: 凭借经验 (to rely on experience). It is more formal than 凭.

column5: The surface of the lake is very calm.
column6: 平静 means calm and still: 心情平静 (a calm mood), 平静地说 (to say calmly).

column4: 我们班的平均成绩是八十分。
column5: Our class's average score is eighty.
column6: 平均 is the average: 平均成绩 (the average score), 平均年龄 (the average age), 平均每天 (on average every day). As a verb it means to divide equally.

column5: The phone's screen is very big.
column6: 屏幕 is a screen: 手机屏幕, 电脑屏幕, 大屏幕 (a big screen).

column4: 这个网上平台有很多课程。
column5: This online platform has many courses.
column6: 平台 is a platform: 网络平台 (an online platform), 学习平台 (a learning platform). It is also a raised flat place.

column5: Do not destroy the environment.
column6: 破坏 is to damage or ruin: 破坏环境 (to damage the environment), 破坏关系 (to ruin a relationship), 破坏东西 (to break things).

column5: Mobile phones are now widespread.
column6: 普及 is to spread widely so that most people can use or get it: 普及教育 (to make education available to all), 已经普及 (already widespread).

column5: I am looking forward to your letter.
column6: 期待 is to look forward to something: 期待着 (looking forward), 令人期待 (exciting to look forward to).
